summary: Routing fallback loop triggered by model-pin grace-period mismatch during canary drain shift
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary drain-shift in us-east the customer's pinned-model sessions began bouncing between the pinned variant and fallback variants, producing a sustained routing loop. The loop caused repeated model switches for in-flight sessions and elevated 5xx and latency for affected tenants.

Impact:
- Multiple tenants on a dedicated pool (OrionMaps) observed mixed outputs and elevated error rates for ~18 minutes.
- Production traffic experienced token-latency spikes (median +120ms) and 502/504 counts increased.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool (dedicated), us-east region, host cluster rp-prod-ded-3
- Canary rollout in progress for model openchat-7b-v2 -> openchat-7b-v2-quant (weight shift 10% -> 50%)

Observed at 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z in customer telemetry and platform metrics.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a weighted canary promote of model variant v2-quant in a dedicated pool (10% -> 50% over 10m).
2) Trigger a graceful drain shift of a hot node (scale down / drain with grace-period 30s) overlapping the canary window,
3) Replay a cohort of pinned session tokens bound to the older variant while the router re-evaluates pin tokens and fallback policies.
4) Observe routing decisions and token logs at the edge proxy and router reconciliation endpoints.
observed_behavior: Router TTL and pin grace-period are mismatched: pin tokens on edge proxies expired later than router's in-memory pin lease, causing router to consider the session unpinned and route to fallback variant. The edge continued to present a pin token, router accepted the request, then later re-evaluated on health probes and re-routed back to pinned variant — creating repeated switch attempts and a fallback loop.
expected_behavior: During overlap of drain/shifts and canary weight change, the router and edge proxies should have consistent pin lease semantics so a session remains pinned until a single coherent handoff completes (no repeated switch attempts). Router should not short-circuit pinned sessions mid-request or flip precedence more than once per session lifecycle.
logs: [09:12:06Z] serving-runtime/node-3: healthprobe=failed draining=true; node removed from pool
Error excerpts: 502: "model backend connection reset" correlated with immediate prior route flip
comments: 2026-03-10T09:20:00Z - Support (Anika Patel): Customer reported intermittent mixed outputs after canary promote. Attached request ids and timestamps. Asked for tracing and timeline.

2026-03-10T09:32:12Z - SRE (Diego Ramos): Identified spike in router re-evaluations coincident with node drain events. Pin lease TTL on router ephemeral cache set to 20s while edge cookie grace set to 90s. Hypothesis: lease mismatch leads to flip-flop.
2026-03-10T10:01:45Z - ENG (Maya Chen): Runbook done: pinned session debugging. Gathering router logs and KV cache snapshots. Noted router had aggressive background re-check after node removal.
2026-03-10T11:05:00Z - Support (Anika Patel): Shared customer mitigation: temporarily paused canary weight change and queued further rollouts until fix. Customer accepted workaround pending RCA.
2026-03-12T14:10:00Z - ENG (Diego Ramos): Working on coordinated TTL alignment patch and extra guard to prevent re-route if request has pin_token header and original route succeeded within last 60s.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Router in-memory pin lease shorter than edge cookie grace. When the node drains, router marks local lease expired and re-routes to fallback variant; edge still sends pin token leading to acceptance and later re-evaluation.
Hypothesis 2: Canary-coordinator triggered a background rebalancer that prompted router to aggressively re-resolve pins for cohorts tied to the drained node, amplifying flip frequency.

Findings: Correlation matrix shows re-route events cluster around node drain start and completion. Router config shows pin_lease_ttl=20s, edge cookie grace configured at 90s on the customer's dedicated pool. Canary coordinator re-eval interval observed at 15s causing overlap with router TTL windows.

Partial root cause: Inconsistent TTL semantics across edge/router/canary-coordinator; also missing a request-safety guard that should avoid changing a route mid-request when pin_token present and connection to previous backend was healthy.
Risk: High for any overlapping rollouts and drain operations in dedicated pools where operators tune local grace periods; could cause customer-visible quality degradation and transient errors.
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-10T10:15Z): Pause ongoing canary weight adjustments and postpone scheduled node drains for the affected dedicated pool. Instruct customer to avoid concurrent drain+promote windows.

Hotfix (deployed 2026-03-12): Align router pin_lease_ttl with edge cookie grace by default for dedicated pools and add a request-safety guard: if request includes a valid pin_token and the previous route returned a successful backend response within N seconds, do not re-route mid-request. Patch rolled to canary routers with a staged rollout 20% -> 100% over 2h.

Follow-up: Add telemetry alert for pin_lease_ttl mismatch across components and update runbook to require coordinated TTL settings on dedicated pools. Engineering to add an e2e test for drain+canary overlap to prevent regressions. Customer notified and will monitor for 48 hours.
